summary: Execute independent engineering acceptance while live completion remains bounded by the authorized allowance. The live e-IP run produced five real candidates and Java checks, but its refinement referenced a nonexistent source unit and correctly failed acceptance. The counted repair path, six-call pilot budget and adversarial cases are now part of this regression.
findings: Live call accounting: twelve invocations are already consumed, including access/startup failures; the authorized ledger ceiling is sixteen. No refunds or silent ceiling changes are allowed, and four slots remain below the six-call complete-attempt budget.
A generation pass is not enough: P5 still requires successful refinement, reconstruction and two retained-source cases. P6 does not override this unmet criterion.
Real failure repaired in code: invalid output receives a separately reserved fresh-context correction with the exact error and allowed source IDs. Repair count and issue-root caps still apply.
Probe bias repaired: truncated Cartesian probes could keep early facts unknown in every test. Known baselines and single-fact boundary changes now precede Cartesian filling.
New endpoints require server-authorized provider access; callers cannot supply shell commands or arbitrary model adapters.
Argument groups and entropy describe retained branches. Complete-link grouping requires checked formal pairs; none confer legal authority.
Independent annotation labels require different registered reviewers and adjudication; source replacement invalidates a pending freeze. No actual human reference corpus is claimed.
